Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

severe adjective

of a person: strict, stern

also strict, stern, harsh (of a person), severity, strictness, a strict father, hard on (someone), he was hard on me, austere, callous, insensitive, tough, callousness, harshness, insensitivity, rude (of character), rough

classical

Ter. Heaut. 1023: quam sevērus!
Cic. Lael. 95: cīvis sevērus et gravis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 158, 146

sevērus, sevēra, sevērum

adjective

strict, stern, grave

Grave and strict in look and conduct; of judges, stern; of people who live soberly, austere (Catull. 27.6). Severity is sevēritās (Tac. Agr. 9.4). Only rarely in a bad sense, harsh (Lewis & Short). It also means serious, not joking (see serious).

Other words

  • dūrus, dūra, dūrum — hard, harsh, unbending (of a person)

    adjective · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 439: satis jam satis pater dūrus fuī; Ter. Ph. 497: adeōne ingeniō esse dūrō tē atque inexōrābilī …?; Traupman 150, 153, 154, 158

    Its first sense is hard to the touch (see hard). Of a person, hard and unbending, where sevērus is strict but just; a father is dūrus in Terence when he has been too harsh.

  • austērus, austēra, austērum — stern, strict; of taste, harsh, dry

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Cael. 33: illō austērō mōre ac modō (Lewis & Short); Quint. 2.2.5: nōn austēritās ejus trīstis; Traupman 149

    From Greek αὐστηρός: of wine and fruit, harsh and dry to the taste (Cato, Celsus); of a person or a style, stern and unsmiling. Not before Cicero in this sense (Lewis & Short).

  • dūritia, dūritiae f. — hardness: harshness, callousness

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 150, 153, 154

  • asper, aspera, asperum — rough, harsh, stern

    also used · classical · Traupman 149, 157, 158

  • acerbus, acerba, acerbum — harsh, bitter; strict (of someone in authority)

    also used · classical · Traupman 158

Examples

  • Sed ipse ēgreditur: quam sevērus!

    But here he comes out himself: how stern he looks!Ter. Heaut. 1023

  • Nōn possum: satis jam satis pater dūrus fuī.

    I can’t: I have been a harsh father long enough, more than enough.Ter. Heaut. 439

  • vīvāmus, mea Lesbia, atque amēmus, rūmōrēsque senum sevēriōrum omnēs ūnius aestimēmus assis!

    let us live, my Lesbia, and love, and value all the mutterings of stern old men at a single penny!Catull. 5.1–3

  • ipse nec habeat vitia nec ferat. nōn austēritās ejus trīstis, nōn dissolūta sit cōmitās

    let the teacher have no faults and put up with none; let his strictness not be gloomy, nor his friendliness slackQuint. 2.2.5

  • In mē dūrus erat.

    He was hard on me.Traupman 100

See also severe, serious, hard.
